title: Label every control, never the placeholder
intent: Keep the field's purpose visible after the user has typed into it.
when_to_use: any field that holds a value the user can edit later
any field where an error must be shown in place
when_not_to_use: a single field search in a persistent toolbar, where an icon and an accessible name carry the purpose
a filter chip row where the control text itself is the label
rules: every input has a visible label bound by for and id; an icon only search field carries an accessible name instead
the placeholder is either absent or holds an example value, and it never repeats the field name
an error message replaces the helper text in place and is tied to the field with aria-describedby
the required state is visible before submission, not only after a failed attempt
trade_off: Visible labels cost vertical space and make dense forms taller, and a placeholder styled form will look cleaner in the first screenshot while failing the second use.
failure_mode: Labels are added but never bound, so they are not announced, and the placeholder keeps the only copy of the expected format, which disappears the moment the user types.

example.brief: Invoice form for a bookkeeper entering many records.
example.ruling: Every field keeps a bound visible label, the placeholder shows a format example only, and an invalid amount replaces the helper line with the error text and aria-describedby to the same field.
